scope: Static analysis of the exact 3.0.2 Build 241129 Rel.3n ARM userspace; no live-device traffic was generated.

components.rpmServer: Consumes the public libmobile API while serving the web-facing JSON RPC socket.
components.libmobile.so: Provides typed getters/setters, reads shared records through libdata_management, and implements an asynchronous Unix-datagram event client.
components.mobile: Owns the server side of the mobile event channel and updates shared modem state.
components.libdata_management.so: Numbered shared/configuration record abstraction used by many libmobile getters; storage and synchronization internals remain unresolved.
components.libmarvellril.so: RIL/AT-facing modem control implementation below the mobile daemon.

sockets.transport: AF_UNIX datagram (confirmed by socket/bind/sendto/recvfrom call paths)
sockets.note: The mobile daemon also contains /tmp/mobile_msg_server.sock; the exact relationship between that name and /tmp/mp_svr_file remains unresolved.

evidence: CMobileEvent::Serialize writes object fields +0x50, +0x54 and +0x5c as three 32-bit words, then copies +0x5c bytes from the buffer at +0x58.
CMobileEvent::Unserialize rejects inputs shorter than 12 bytes and validates total length against 12 plus the third word.
CreateEvent generates a nonzero value at +0x50; request-list lookup and response completion match that field.

read_path.pattern: Many getters instantiate CCfgHelper with a count and numbered record IDs, call GetConfig, and copy typed CCfgItem values into the public result structure.

example.result: Copies a presence/status byte and a bounded 16-byte value into MP_SimIMSI; device-specific contents were neither extracted nor recorded.

composite_status.important_correction: GetAllStatus is a local aggregate over eight libmobile getters, not one monolithic request to the modem daemon. Other web status fields are added by rpmServer and other subsystems.

limits: Numeric configuration record IDs are internal data-model keys, not web RPC module/action IDs.
The symbol-backed event-ID map is recorded in mobile-events.json; some payload structures remain unresolved.
Static presence of setters does not establish web reachability, authorization, persistence, or safety.
No event datagrams were sent to either the sandbox or the physical device during this analysis.
